questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.2 mol/dm³ NaOH reacts with HCl: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. How many moles of HCl are needed?
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = c × V = 0.2 × 0.025 = 0.005 mol. From the equation, the NaOH:HCl ratio is 1:1, so 0.005 mol of HCl is needed.

questions.stem: What volume of 0.5 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid is needed to neutralise 20 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ NaOH? (H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O)
questions.explanation: Moles of NaOH = 1 × 0.02 = 0.02 mol. From the equation, 2 mol NaOH requires 1 mol H₂SO₄, so moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.02/2 = 0.01 mol. Volume = n/c = 0.01/0.5 = 0.02 dm³ = 20 cm³.
